title: Company-wide policies and processes (Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendor, Travel, Templates)
author: Jordan Alvarez
content:
Purpose
This document consolidates company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel and expense policies, and the canonical set of internal templates. It is intended for all Redwood employees, contractors, and hiring managers.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood business units and legal entities unless a separate restricted policy is published.
- Does not replace department-level runbooks or technical procedures where those exist; it defines the corporate guardrails and approval flows.

Key principles
- Least privilege: Access is granted at the minimum necessary level and reviewed regularly.
- Transparency: Changes and procurements should have an auditable trail of approvals.
- Risk-based controls: More sensitive data and systems require stronger controls and approvals.
- Cost-consciousness: Procurement and travel should balance cost with business need.

1) Access & Permissions
Overview
Access requests (systems, cloud projects, SSO groups) must follow the access lifecycle: request -> approval -> provisioning -> periodic review -> revocation.
Roles & responsibilities
- Requester: Submits justification and business owner.
- Approver: Manager or system owner (must be named in approver list).
- IT/Security: Performs provisioning, audit, and quarterly reviews.

Standard process (for new access)
1. Requester opens an Access Request in the IT service portal (link: /ops/access-request). Include justification, duration, and emergency access needs.
2. Manager approval: Manager reviews and approves or rejects within 48 hours.
3. System owner approval (if different): Verifies scope and approves.
4. Provisioning: IT performs provisioning and records the ticket with role granted.
5. Temporary access: When access is time-limited, a deprovisioning date must be set.
6. Quarterly review: System owners review and certify active users.
Access change types & approvals (approval matrix)
- Low risk (e.g., read-only marketing dashboards): manager approval.
- Medium risk (developer access to non-production infra): manager + infra owner.
- High risk (production admin, secrets, key management): manager + infra owner + security team approval.
Emergency access (break-glass)
- Break-glass access may be requested via the on-call security channel. Approval by the on-call SRE + security on-call required. All break-glass sessions must be recorded and reviewed within 24 hours.

2) Change Management
Overview
All changes to production systems, network, security controls, or billing-critical systems follow the change management workflow: request -> risk assessment -> approval -> scheduled deployment -> post-deploy validation -> rollback / postmortem if needed.
Change categories
- Standard changes (pre-approved low-risk recurring tasks): follow the standard change template.
- Minor changes: require change request and manager sign-off.
- Major changes (affecting production availability, security, or cost > $10k): require CAB (Change Advisory Board) review.
Change request checklist
- Owner and roll-back plan
- Expected customer impact and SLOs affected (e.g., latency, error budget)
- Monitoring and alerting to validate the change
- Communication plan (status page, Slack channels, stakeholders)
Scheduling & blackout windows
- Production change windows are Monday–Friday 09:00–17:00 PT unless an emergency. Weekend deployments require CAB approval unless pre-authorized.
Post-change validation & postmortems
- Deploy owner must run the validation checklist within 30 minutes of deployment. Failures escalate to incident process. Any change that causes an outage requires a postmortem within 72 hours.

3) Data Management & Governance
Overview
This section defines data classification, handling, retention, and access approval for company and customer data.
Data classification
- Public: Safe for any external publication.
- Internal: Redwood employees and contractors only.
- Confidential: Business-sensitive (financial plans, non-public roadmaps).
- Restricted: Customer data subject to contractual/regulatory controls (PII, regulated industry data).
Data handling controls
- Encryption: All data at rest and in transit must be encrypted (TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 for at rest where supported).
- Storage location: Customer data subject to residency requirements must be tagged and routed to compliant regions.
- Masking/anonymization: Use for non-production environments. No production PII in dev unless expressly approved and masked.
Retention & deletion
- Default retention: logs 365 days, backups 90 days, analytics derived data 2 years unless a contract specifies otherwise.
- Data deletion requests: Routed to Data Governance team via /ops/data-requests. Approval required from Data Owner and Security.
Data access review
- Quarterly reviews for all high-sensitivity datasets. Data owners must certify access lists.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Overview
Procurement includes purchases of software, cloud spend commitments, hardware, and services. Expenses include T&E and small operational purchases.
Approval thresholds (examples)
- Up to $2,500: Manager approval (purchase card/expense claim).
- $2,501–$50,000: Dept head approval + finance review.
- > $50,000: Exec approval (VP) + procurement + finance + legal review.
Procurement process (steps)
1. Raise a Purchase Requisition in the procurement portal with business justification and expected budget code.
2. Procurement/Finance performs vendor due diligence (see vendor checklist below).
3. Approvals are routed based on threshold.
4. Purchase Order (PO) issued; supplier onboards to accounts payable.
5. Receipt & verification: Requester confirms receipt and submits invoice to AP.
Expense & travel reimbursements
- Use the expense tool to submit receipts within 30 days. Meals and local transport require receipts; per diem allowed where applicable. Non-compliant expenses are subject to manager denial and potential payroll recovery.

5) Vendor Management & Third-party Onboarding
Overview
All vendors must be onboarded via the vendor management process to ensure legal, security, and financial controls are applied.
Vendor onboarding checklist
- Business justification and owner
- Contract review by legal (standard T&Cs or exceptions)
- Security assessment level (light/medium/high) and required controls (pen tests, SOC 2, encryption)
- Data processing agreement (if handling customer data)
- PO and payment terms
- Vendor contact and escalation list
Ongoing vendor reviews
- Annual review for strategic/high-risk vendors. Standard vendors (non-critical, low spend) reviewed every two years.
Termination and offboarding
- Revoke access (SSO, cloud accounts, API keys) immediately upon contract end. Ensure return or deletion of Redwood data per contract terms.

6) Travel Policy (Business travel & reimbursements)
Booking & approvals
- All business travel must be pre-approved by the traveler’s manager. International travel requires travel advisory check with security.
- Use corporate travel portal (link: /ops/travel) for booking to capture company-negotiated rates.
Allowable expenses & limits
- Economy or business class rules: Domestic flights economy; international >8 hours may allow business with VP approval.
- Hotel: Reasonable single room; prefer negotiated partners.
- Meals: Per-diem caps vary by city; itemized receipts required for meals > $75.
Reimbursement process
- Submit expenses within 30 days with receipts. Manager approves, finance processes within next payroll cycle.
Safety & duty of care
- Employees traveling on company business are enrolled in the duty-of-care program. Report security incidents to security@redwood.com immediately.

7) Internal Templates & Forms
Available templates (links are in the template library)
- Access request form (access-request-template.md)
- Change request template (change-request-template.md)
- Vendor onboarding checklist (vendor-onboarding-template.md)
- Purchase requisition template (po-requisition-template.xlsx)
- Travel & expense claim template (expense-claim-template.xlsx)
Usage guidance
- Templates are canonical and should be used as the starting point for requests and approvals. Tailor only when necessary and include approver sign-off when deviating from the template.

8) Exceptions & Change Requests to these Policies
- Any exception to these policies requires a documented exception request routed to the policy owner (people-ops) and relevant stakeholders (security, finance, legal). Exceptions must include compensating controls and a defined expiry date.

9) Monitoring, Compliance, and Audit
- Internal audits: People-ops and Internal Audit will run annual checks of policy adherence (access reviews, procurement approvals, vendor documentation).
- Security & Compliance: Runs quarterly reviews for high-risk systems and data. Findings are tracked in the remediation tracker and assigned owners.

Notes
